display.purpose: Exactly one per page: the hero h1, capped at 17ch. The only type above 20px in the system.

headline.purpose: Section h2. The working ceiling for everything below the hero.

title.purpose: Card h3, step h4, schema frame titles.

body.purpose: Reading prose at 78ch; leads use the same size in --muted at 74ch.

body-dense.purpose: Card and step copy where density beats comfort.

label.purpose: Mono micro-labels: eyebrows, callout header strips, table headers, nav group headers, legends, footers.

figure.purpose: The four hero statistics only. Tabular sans numerals inside a mono cell.

code.purpose: Code blocks and the inspector drawer's source view.

shadows.name: bench
shadows.purpose: The only shadow on the page body. Cards, callouts, lifecycle nodes, schema frames, the hero principle line. Light theme: 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / .10).

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: Reserved for the one element that leaves the page plane: the slide-in file viewer. Light theme: 0 8px 28px rgb(0 0 0 / .16).

motion.name: drawer-slide
motion.purpose: The inspector drawer entering from the right edge.

motion.name: scrim-fade
motion.purpose: The flat 60% black backdrop. Dimmed, never blurred.

motion.name: anchor-scroll
motion.purpose: In-page navigation from the rail and from clickable schema nodes.

surfaceTextures.name: dot-lattice
surfaceTextures.purpose: The infinite canvas under the page and inside every schema frame.

surfaceTextures.name: grain
surfaceTextures.purpose: Kills banding on the near-black ground. Never above 3%.

constraints: Both pages open from a local clone over file://: everything inline, no remote font, CSS, JS or image, ever.
Both themes are required; the pre-paint theme script stays in <head> to avoid a flash.
START_HERE keeps its data-file chips, its slide-in file viewer, and its links to BOARD_SETUP.
BOARD_SETUP must contain no data-file attributes.
tests/test-board-guide.sh pins ~50 factual prose claims in BOARD_SETUP; they must survive verbatim.
tools/embed-files.py must be re-run after any edit to START_HERE.html; CI fails on payload drift.

components.description: The only button in the system. Theme toggle, schema expand, drawer close.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { padding: 7px 10px; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; background: var(--raised, #262626); border: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); font-size: 11px; font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: var(--ink, #FAFAFA); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #3FBF52); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Signal Chip
components.description: Outlined, tinted status tag. Variants recolor text and border only, never the fill.
components.html: auto gated escalate opus
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: .04em; background: var(--raised, #262626); color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); border: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); white-space: nowrap; font-family: var(--sans, Inter, sans-serif); } .ds-chip-live { color: var(--accent-text, #3FBF52); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent, #3FBF52) 40%, var(--line, #333333)); } .ds-chip-human { color: var(--warn, #E0A32E); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--warn, #E0A32E) 40%, var(--line, #333333)); } .ds-chip-esc { color: var(--negative-text, #E86A5A); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--negative, #E0503F) 40%, var(--line, #333333)); }

components.name: Node Card
components.description: The workhorse container. Status dot instead of a pictogram, dense 13.5px body.
components.html:
A place per work item

One card per epic, carrying an id in its title. The full record travels as JSON inside the card.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--surface, #1C1C1C); border: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); border-radius: 10px; padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / .5); font-family: var(--sans, Inter, sans-serif); max-width: 340px; } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0 0 6px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25; letter-spacing: -.01em; color: var(--ink, #FAFAFA); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; } .ds-card p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); font-size: 13.5px; line-height: 1.55; } .ds-ic { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); flex: 0 0 auto; }

components.name: Callout
components.description: The system's aside: a raised header strip with a bottom hairline, a mono label and a status dot. Never a left accent bar.
components.html:
The split everything rests on

The board shows state. Your approvals are read from the forge — the pull request — never from the board.
components.css: .ds-callout { margin: 16px 0; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--surface, #1C1C1C); border: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); max-width: 78ch; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / .5); font-family: var(--sans, Inter, sans-serif); } .ds-callout-lbl { font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 500; color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; background: var(--raised, #262626); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); padding: 6px 14px; } .ds-callout-lbl::before { content: ""; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); flex: 0 0 auto; } .ds-callout p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.65; padding: 12px 14px; } .ds-callout-ok .ds-callout-lbl { color: var(--accent-text, #3FBF52); } .ds-callout-ok .ds-callout-lbl::before { background: var(--accent, #3FBF52); } .ds-callout-warn .ds-callout-lbl { color: var(--warn, #E0A32E); } .ds-callout-warn .ds-callout-lbl::before { background: var(--warn, #E0A32E); } .ds-callout-danger .ds-callout-lbl { color: var(--negative-text, #E86A5A); } .ds-callout-danger .ds-callout-lbl::before { background: var(--negative, #E0503F); }

components.name: Rail Navigation

components.html:
Step by step
LinearNotionJira

components.name: Statistics Strip
components.description: The first-viewport evidence band: hairline gutters made of the 1px gap over a --line background.
components.html: 962 assertions across 39 suites26 ADRs · immutable once accepted12 lifecycle states4 runtimes
components.css: .ds-badges { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); gap: 1px; background: var(--line, #333333); border: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); border-radius: 10px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-badge { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; padding: 13px 16px; background: var(--surface, #1C1C1C); font-size: 10.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); } .ds-badge b { color: var(--ink, #FAFAFA); font-size: 22px; line-height: 1.1; font-weight: 500; font-family: var(--sans, Inter, sans-serif); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: -.02em; } @media (max-width: 960px) { .ds-badges { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); } }

components.name: Lifecycle Node
components.description: One of twelve states in a horizontally scrolling row. The status dot carries the whole semantic load.
components.css: .ds-lc { width: 150px; border: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); border-radius: 10px; padding: 10px 12px; background: var(--surface, #1C1C1C); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 5px; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / .5); } .ds-lc-st { font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--ink, #FAFAFA); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; } .ds-lc-st::before { content: ""; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); flex: 0 0 auto; } .ds-lc p { margin: 0; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); line-height: 1.45; font-family: var(--sans, Inter, sans-serif); } .ds-lc-who { font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 9.5px; color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); margin-top: auto; padding-top: 6px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); } .ds-lc-you .ds-lc-st::before { background: var(--warn, #E0A32E); } .ds-lc-rework .ds-lc-st::before { background: var(--negative, #E0503F); } .ds-lc-done .ds-lc-st::before { background: var(--accent, #3FBF52); }

components.css: .ds-fchip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 3px 8px; border-radius: 6px; font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); background: var(--raised, #262626); border: 1px solid var(--line, #333333); cursor: pointer; } .ds-fchip::before { content: ""; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--line, #333333); flex: 0 0 auto; } .ds-fchip:hover { color: var(--ink, #FAFAFA); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent, #3FBF52) 40%, var(--line, #333333)); } .ds-fchip:hover::before { background: var(--accent, #3FBF52); } .ds-fchip-dir::before { border-radius: 2px; } .ds-flabel { font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 9.5px; letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted, #8C8C8C); font-weight: 500; margin-right: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
This is a bench you inspect, not a brochure you scroll. Two long documents are laid out like instrument panels sitting on an infinite dotted work surface: near-black ground, matte graphite cards, hairline rules, and machine-facing strings set in mono so a config key never has to pretend to be prose. Nothing is lit from within. Nothing glows. The reader is a skeptic evaluating whether an autonomous agent can be trusted with their repo, and the visual register has to match the product's own voice: exact, unshowy, willing to state its own limits.

The palette is almost entirely neutral, and that is load-bearing rather than austere. Because the ground is graphite and the type is grey-on-black, the single green reads as an instrument light: it means live signal — a merge, a happy exit, a feedback edge that actually loops. Amber means a human moment. Red means a gate or a hazard. Those three chromatic slots are the entire color vocabulary; everything else is a neutral step. Density is deliberately high — many small true facts, packed at a 13.5–15px reading size — because the reader is technical and already warm.

The world explicitly refuses the dark-SaaS landing page: no gradient hero, no neon-on-black gloss, no frosted glass, no backdrop-filter, no colored glow behind a call to action. Depth comes from one tonal ladder (--bg to --surface to --raised) plus one tight shadow, not from light. The system ships in both light and dark, driven by a data-theme attribute on <html> with the dark theme as default, because the pages are opened from a local clone and must respect the machine they land on.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas under a 24px radial dot lattice, at 10% white (dark) / 13% black (light)
One rationed green for live signal; amber for human moments; red for gates
1px --line hairlines everywhere; corners are 6/8/10px, never pill-shaped
Mono for every machine-facing string — paths, env vars, states, counts, micro-labels
One tight shadow (0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / .5)), no second elevation on the page body
A 3% fractal-noise grain overlay to kill banding on the near-black ground; never above 3%
Fully inline and self-contained: no remote font, stylesheet, script or image, ever

rules.name: The Rationed Green Rule
rules.body: Green means live signal — merged, verified, the loop closing. If an element is not reporting a live positive state, it does not get the accent. A page where green appears more than a handful of times has stopped meaning anything.

rules.name: The Three Slots Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red. That is the whole chromatic vocabulary; no fourth hue is introduced for any reason, and no hue is introduced by the light theme.

rules.name: The Type-Only Lift Rule
rules.body: #E0503F is for borders, dots and wires; #E86A5A is for glyphs. Never swap them — the pinned red fails AA at label sizes, and the lifted red is wrong on a 1px stroke.

rules.name: The Same Family Rule
rules.body: The light theme is the same neutral ramp inverted, not a second palette. Only --accent-text, --warn and --negative shift value, and only to clear contrast on white.

rules.name: The Twenty-Pixel Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Below the hero, nothing exceeds 20px. The one h1 per page is the entire exception; there is no second large moment anywhere on either document.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Machine Rule
rules.body: Mono marks machine-facing strings and micro-labels only. Micro-labels are mono at 10px with .06em tracking — never tracked uppercase sans, which is the generic-dashboard tell this world refuses.

rules.name: The Reading Body Rule
rules.body: Body copy is 15px in --ink, not the 12px --muted of a node canvas. These are documents that must be read end to end, and the reading size is the deviation that makes that honest.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two shadows. Anything on the page uses the bench shadow or none; only the overlay drawer uses the far shadow. No hover shadow, no focus shadow, no colored shadow.

rules.name: The No-Light Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this world emits light. Glow, gradient fills, glass and backdrop blur are all absent from the build and stay absent — depth is tone plus a hairline.

dos: Do keep everything inline and self-contained. Both pages open from a local clone over file://; no remote font, stylesheet, script, image or analytics may ever be added.
Do ship both themes. Every new token needs a light value in the :root[data-theme="light"] block, and the pre-paint theme script must stay in <head> so there is no flash.
Do ration the green to live signal, and keep amber for human moments and red for gates.
Do use --negative-text for red glyphs and --negative for red borders, dots and wires.
Do set every machine-facing string in mono — paths, env vars, config keys, state names, counts, micro-labels.
Do build depth from the --bg to --surface to --raised ladder plus a 1px --line hairline, and reach for the bench shadow only when something should read as an object.
Do hold the radius scale at 4 / 6 / 8 / 10px and border every surface at exactly 1px.
Do re-run tools/embed-files.py after any edit to START_HERE.html — CI fails on payload drift.
Do preserve START_HERE's data-file chips, its slide-in file viewer, and its links to BOARD_SETUP.
Do leave BOARD_SETUP free of any data-file attribute, and leave its ~50 pinned factual claims verbatim — tests/test-board-guide.sh asserts them.
donts: Don't add a glow, a gradient fill, a glass panel or a backdrop-filter. The scrim is dimmed, never blurred.
Don't introduce a fourth hue, a second accent, or a hue in the light ramp.
Don't exceed 20px anywhere below the hero, and don't add a second display-scale moment to a page.
Don't raise the grain overlay above 3%.
Don't add a third shadow, a hover shadow, or a colored shadow.
Don't use a saturated filled pill for a chip, or a filled/accented button — buttons are ghost, chips are outlined and tinted.
Don't put a pictogram, emoji or icon-font glyph where a status dot belongs; monoline geometry or nothing.
Don't mark an aside with a left accent bar — callouts use the header-strip node anatomy.
Don't set micro-labels in tracked uppercase sans; they are mono.
Don't re-route the schema wires as beziers; orthogonal runs with solid triangular heads are the diagram language.
